cross_cutting.content:
# deploy-gtm-agent

A go-to-market strategy agent deployed withdeepagents deploy. Given a product or feature, it coordinates a sync market-researcher subagent and an async content-writer subagent to produce a full GTM plan with supporting marketing materials.

This example demonstrates the sync/async subagent pattern: market research blocks on results before strategy is written, while content creation runs in the background and is integrated when ready.

## Prerequisites

Variable | Description 
---|---
OPENAI_API_KEY | Model access (gpt-5.4-nano) 
LANGSMITH_API_KEY | Required for deploy 

Copy.env and fill in your keys.

## Deploy
deepagents deploy

The subagents defined undersubagents/ are automatically discovered and wired in at deploy time.

## What to try

Once deployed, open the agent in LangSmith and send it prompts like:

- "We're launching a new Python SDK for AI agents next month — build me a GTM plan"
- "Help us position our vector database product against Pinecone and Weaviate"
- "We're targeting mid-market engineering teams — what channels should we prioritize?"

The agent will kick off market research, synthesize a strategy, and produce content briefs in parallel.

## Query via SDK
from langgraph_sdk import get_client

client = get_client(url="https://<your-deployment-url>")
thread = await client.threads.create()

async for chunk in client.runs.stream(
    thread["thread_id"], "agent",
    input={"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Build a GTM plan for our new Python SDK for AI agents"}]},
    stream_mode="messages",
):
    print(chunk.data, end="", flush=True)

Find your deployment URL in LangSmith under Deployments. See the LangGraph SDK docs for more.

## Structure
deploy-gtm-agent/
├── AGENTS.md              # Supervisor agent instructions
├── deepagents.toml        # Deploy config (model)
├── mcp.json               # MCP server config
├── skills/
│   └── competitor-analysis/   # Competitor analysis skill
└── subagents/
    └── market-researcher/     # Sync subagent for market research
        ├── AGENTS.md
        ├── deepagents.toml
        └── skills/
            └── analyze-market/

cross_cutting.title: How Runable builds an agent for small business owners and tracks everything in PostHog
cross_cutting.description: How Runable ... tracks everything in PostHog Runable is an AI platform that turns natural language prompts into apps, websites, pitch decks, ad campaigns, and more. ... Their first step was setting up Product Analytics and Session Replay, to see where people got stuck in the product.
cross_cutting.content:
# How Runable builds an agent for small business owners and tracks everything in PostHog

Runable is an AI platform that turns natural language prompts into apps, websites, pitch decks, ad campaigns, and more. The company recently closed a $21M Series A – momentum that’s reflected in their product data sent to PostHog: event volume surged from 317k in August 2025 to 40M in August 2026.

Most of Runable's users are small business owners who want to leverage AI without setting up agents or API keys. "Almost 80% of the world still doesn’t use agents," says Eshaan Pawan, Head of Growth. "Because it's hard."

When Runable started in mid-2025, no one knew what a general-purpose agent should look like. "Last year, it was still pretty new to anyone outside the AI sphere," says Ankit Kumar, an SDE at Runable. With no playbook to copy, the team had to learn from how people actually used it.

Their first step was setting up Product Analytics and Session Replay, to see where people got stuck in the product. Error Tracking and Logs followed for debugging, then Feature Flags to safely roll out new features.

For Ankit, LLM traces in AI Observability were the big win. "The main feature in Runable is the agent run – how the agent is responding to user messages," he says. His team needs to see where runs get stuck in order to set engineering priorities. In addition to using the default AIO dashboard to track cost, latency, tokens, and error rate across models, features, and users, they build a dashboard for each failure mode, fix the worst issues first, then focus on cutting token use and tuning caching.

<OSQuote customer="runable" author="ankit_kumar" quote={0} />

## Testing big changes with small rollouts

In February, Runable tried a pricing page that built a custom plan around each user's use case instead of offering four or five fixed ones. It went out behind a feature flag to 10 to 20% of users, and the data showed it hurt conversion.

"We noticed that users found the UI a bit confusing," Ankit says. About six weeks in, they scrapped it. "That decision was totally dependent on feature flags and event tracking in PostHog." Since only a slice of users ever saw it, there was no announcement to walk back and no flood of complaints – just a flag to turn off.

That's how most things ship at Runable, which has 39 flags live in production right now. A new model that's better for one kind of user can be worse for another, so the team doesn't ship everything to everyone at once. They split their ICP into personas such as freelancers, social media creators, and first-timers. Traces and events show what each segment is prompting for, so new features go out behind flags to the group they suit best.

The growth team uses flags too, for dynamic pricing and credits. An agent sets them up, then Eshaan checks the logic in the PostHog Web UI. "It's directly impacting the product," he says. "I can't leave it to the agent completely."

## A refreshing use of dashboards

At his last company, Eshaan worked with 40 to 50 people whose whole job was tying acquisition data to retention and product analytics. At Runable, he does the same work with a team of two. "Ankit set up the product metrics and I set up the acquisition metrics," he says. "And that's it. That's our team." He puts that down to having one source of truth: "It has really helped us cut down the number of people required."

Eshaan is a power user of both AI and UI. He might actually be the heaviest dashboard user we've met, with over 500 insight tiles and about 100 he checks four or five times a day. "I'm the guy who's just refreshing all the dashboards every hour," he says. "I'm using it like people use Databricks plus Tableau."

He didn't build them by hand. First, he connected 13 sources to Runable's Context Warehouse, including Stripe, six ad platforms, AppsFlyer, Dub, and the Google Sheets where he logs influencer campaigns. Then he pointed the Runable agent at the PostHog API, with his own config and skills, and had it build the insights.

The result is the whole funnel in one place: impression → page view → sign-up → first prompt → first artifact → free credit limit → paid, broken down by source, country, and device. PostHog also sends his conversion events straight to Google Ads and Meta, so he no longer needs Google Tag Manager.

<OSQuote customer="runable" author="eshaan_pawan" quote={0} />

The rest of Runable's team also uses both the Web UI and agents. 71 people have used PostHog in the last six months (about 30 of them daily), some clicking through insights and some asking an agent to pull the numbers. In the last month alone, their agents made 7,562 tool calls from Claude Code, Codex, and Runable itself. Two thirds were SQL, the rest mostly Logs and Error Tracking: ranking issues by how many users they hit, and pulling exception payloads to find the failing method.

## Session Replay monthly marathon

When the numbers can't explain something, Eshaan watches user behavior directly in Session Replay. Once or twice a month, he blocks off a day to binge recordings. "You're just obsessed with the problem," he says. "If you're not able to get it through data, you have to go and look at the session and see what's wrong."

Ankit's team uses replays the same way, to spot where people get stuck or confused in the UI. That's about to matter even more as Runable rebuilds its whole website (new UI, new internal structure) and moves its agents to a new sandbox provider.

Both will ship the way everything else does at Runable: tested behind flags, watched in replays, and measured on dashboards. It's a setup that covers acquisition, product, retention, and costs, all without a data team. So what would happen if PostHog disappeared tomorrow?

"It would set me back by, like, a month," Eshaan says. "Everything is integrated with PostHog."

<OSQuote customer="runable" author="eshaan_pawan" quote={1} />

cross_cutting.content:
# Netron網創資訊推出NAVI 3.0企業AI生產力平台

Netron網創資訊總經理吳炳鈞強調「NAVI3.0能為為企業構築兼具提升生產力與堅實資安防禦力的長期競爭護城河」。Netron網創資訊

隨著人工智慧（AI）技術由單點內容生成，進化為任務自主執行與跨系統協作，如何將AI轉化為「企業實質生產力」提高企業競爭力，已成為企業決策者推動轉型時的核心課題。

看準企業對工作流程整合、資安合規與成本可控性的剛性需求，雲端暨AI解決方案領導廠商Netron網創資訊宣布推出全新「NAVI 3.0企業AI生產力平台」。該平台以「多Agent（AI代理）自主協作」與「Workflow 工作流程自動化」為核心，搭配彈性雲地部署架構與三層成本防透支護欄，全面突破企業導入AI時面臨的「工具零散、流程斷鏈與成本失控」三大瓶頸；在嚴密保障機敏資料安全的前提下，助企業快速實現規模化團隊生產力。

Netron 網創資訊依據多年企業服務實務觀察指出，企業無法快速導入AI無法的關鍵，在於三大瓶頸：

1. 企業機敏資料無法上雲的資安兩難：企業機敏資料無法上雲的資安兩難：許多產業如金融、製造與高科技等內部擁有極高比例的核心技術代碼、專利與客戶個資，在缺乏彈性混合部署架構下，許多企業在AI導入上未能全面落實。

2. 部門私採工具衍生多重營運成本黑洞：成本黑洞：各部門自行採購多種外部工具缺乏集中控管，使商業機密散落各處；「存取權限如何劃分」、「高風險動作是否受控」以及「Token與預算是否超支」，皆成為管理階層極大的營運風險。

3. AI模型分工細緻開發週期長整合困難：開發週期長整合困難：現有AI模型已逐漸分工化，不同的AI模型有不同的應用場景，如何在內部建立一個工具可以適用不同部門與任務，開發過程實為困難，另外在整合內部資料／系統讓AI真的為己所用亦需要大量整合時間。

NAVI 3.0兼顧「雲地彈性」與「嚴謹治理」 為企業構築三大核心優勢

針對企業決策者的真實痛點，Netron網創資訊總經理吳炳鈞強調：「企業需要的從不是更多功能炫目卻難以管理的『AI科技玩具』，而是一套能實質驅動營收成長、提高組織效能的『企業AI生產力平台』。NAVI 3.0的核心價值，在於讓AI真正落地貫穿各項業務流程，同時將數據主權與成本掌控權牢牢留存於企業內部，為企業構築兼具提升生產力與堅實資安防禦力的長期競爭護城河。」

為回應企業決策者對效率提升與風險控管的雙重標準，NAVI 3.0打造三大核心優勢：

視覺化Workflow引領多Agent自主協作 打造自主運轉智慧工作流

為回應企業決策者對效率提升與風險控管的雙重標準，NAVI 3.0打造了全新一代的智慧升級。首先在協作效率上，系統打破傳統單一AI的限制，實現「多Agent協作與視覺化Workflow」的自主智慧工作流。平台內建涵蓋市場研究、數據分析、商務文案與簡報排版等多組跨職能AI Agent，並提供超過150個預建工作流功能節點。企業不僅能即插即用成熟模板快速上線，更能透過自然語言「一句話畫出Workflow流程草稿」，由AI自動生成專屬Agent職能。

這群AI代理人具備自動交棒與端到端排程能力，能自主協同完成複雜工作，徹底告別繁瑣的人工搬運。更重要的是，系統建立「人機協同審核機制」，可在對外發信、合約與金流審核等關鍵節點設置強制人工核准關卡，並僅在必要時啟用高階模型，完美兼顧決策安全性與成本控制。

彈性雲地部署打破資安僵局 三層配額護欄杜絕預算黑洞

針對企業最頭痛的資安治理，NAVI 3.0推出「彈性雲地部署與企業級資安治理」架構，確保機敏數據不出邊界。系統支援企業自有公有雲、純地端機房（On-Premise）或雲地混合架構，讓敏感任務全面落於企業內部運作，化解法規與資安痛點。在內部管理上，平台依部門與專案嚴格切分權限，落實「無權限者問AI 也查不到」的智慧隔離，並提供完整的操作軌跡日誌（Audit Log）與重要動作確認機制。

此外，為了防止 Token與費用透支，管理者可在後台彈性設定各部門與員工每月的預算上限，透過「三層配額預算護欄」精準控管每筆成本，達標即自動卡關，讓營運風險降至最低。

串接逾30款主流大模型 支援80種跨平台整合無縫對接既有IT

最後，NAVI 3.0展現極高的相容性，具備「多模型智慧切換與多元系統整合」實力，能無縫接軌企業既有的IT生態。系統內建LLM Gateway，無縫調度OpenAI、Anthropic Claude、Google Gemini等超過30款主流大語言模型，使用者可依據文字、影像、語音或文檔解析等不同任務類型，彈性指派最適合的模型。

在企業系統串接方面，NAVI 3.0支援整合各類ERP、CRM等超過80種主流辦公工具，且系統本身即具備 MCP Server（Model Context Protocol）架構，能完美相容外部擴充應用。此舉不僅大幅縮短開發週期，更能延伸保護企業過去的IT投資，讓AI導入真正為己所用。

AI轉型不僅是效率競爭，更是獲利與防禦的體質考驗。以製造業為例，產線人員只需在通訊頻道回報異常，NAVI 3.0即可自動比對知識庫歷史案例、建立工單並指派負責人，大幅節省三至五成的通報與分派作業時間；以金融業為例，只需設定一次自動排程，平台便能每週自動彙整同業動態、法規更新與市場新聞來生成分析簡報。NAVI 3.0兼具雲地彈性、流程自動化與成本護欄，助企業在守牢資安主權與預算控管的前提下，將技術潛能化為可衡量的實質利潤，穩健邁向智慧營運新紀元。

cross_cutting.content:
## SoftBank Group and Grab sign joint development agreements to develop AI infrastructure in Malaysia

- 10 Nov, 2026
- 6 min read

TOKYO and SINGAPORE, 9 November 2026 – SoftBank Group Corp. and Grab Holdings Limited today announced the signing of joint development agreements in connection with plans for $1.85 billion in initial combined seed capital, together with Petroleum Sarawak Berhad, to develop AI infrastructure in Malaysia.

The collaboration aims to establish AI infrastructure in Malaysia to meet the growing demand for computing capacity across Southeast Asia and globally. Once fully operational, the facilities are expected to be amongst the largest AI infrastructure of their kind in Asia, providing governments, multinational companies and small businesses with reliable access to advanced computing capabilities.

The combined investment forms part of a multi-year plan to develop AI compute capacity across Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia, with a long-term target of five gigawatts or more. The proposed initial combined seed capital is $1.85 billion, comprising $1 billion from SoftBank Group, $750 million from Grab and $100 million from PETROS.

The proposed investment will be deployed in stages subject to projects achieving key development and customer contract milestones, and the necessary closing conditions. The parties will also seek additional investors and hyperscaler customers to support project development and expansion.

“AI infrastructure will power the next wave of growth, and Malaysia has the talent and ambition to help lead it. Together with Grab, we will build the capacity needed to support Malaysia’s digital ambitions and accelerate AI innovation across Southeast Asia,” said Masayoshi Son, Chairman and CEO of SoftBank Group Corp.

“Grab’s mission is and always has been the technological advancement and economic development of Southeast Asia. Southeast Asia is one of the world's fastest-growing digital economies, and Grab is at the forefront of developing AI solutions for the region. Together with SoftBank Group, we plan to build critical AI infrastructure in Malaysia, where Grab began, for all of Southeast Asia. This infrastructure will allow us to accelerate the development of localised AI solutions for our communities. Through this partnership, we can drive faster regional AI development and adoption, bringing its transformative benefits to many millions of people, while contributing to Malaysia's economy through the creation of high-value jobs and AI upskilling,” said Anthony Tan, co-founder, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Grab.

Powering Southeast Asia's AI-driven future

Research by Google, Temasek and Bain & Company indicates that per capita AI usage across Southeast Asia's six largest economies is currently around one-tenth of the level in the United States, with regional AI usage projected to scale by up to 60-fold by 2030. Meeting this anticipated demand will require substantial investment in AI infrastructure within the region.

The projects will be developed in close collaboration with Malaysia's Federal Government and the Sarawak Government, aligning with the National AI Action Plan 2026–2030 (AI Nation 2030) to position Malaysia as an inclusive and sustainable AI nation, as well as Sarawak's long-term development aspiration under the Post COVID-19 Development Strategy 2030. The facilities will operate in line with Malaysia’s renewable energy use guidelines, and feature high-efficiency infrastructure designed to reduce water use and reliance on local power grids.

Beyond AI infrastructure development, the parties will explore other areas of mutual interest, including advanced manufacturing in Malaysia. These initiatives are expected to create high-value employment opportunities in engineering, design and technical fields, while supporting the objectives of the National Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR) Policy and the Malaysia Digital Economy Blueprint (MDEB). They will also help accelerate advanced technology adoption, improve productivity and strengthen the capabilities of Malaysia's workforce.

Project overview and investment

The Sarawak project will be jointly developed by SoftBank Group, Grab and PETROS, building on the Framework Agreement signed in Kuching on October 8, 2026. The proposed initial investment in the Sarawak project is $1 billion, comprising $800 million from SoftBank Group, $100 million from Grab and $100 million from PETROS. Grab has an option to increase its stake, which will cause SoftBank Group’s stake to decrease, albeit with SoftBank Group remaining as the majority shareholder.

The proposed initial seed capital for the Peninsular Malaysia project is $850 million, comprising $650 million from Grab and $200 million from SoftBank Group. As the project’s founding shareholder, Grab will lead its development and bring in long-term strategic investors as the project scales, diversifying its funding base. Further development is expected to be funded at the project level through third-party equity and non-recourse project financing.

Anthony Tan is expected to oversee the development of both projects and appoint dedicated management teams to run day-to-day operations while continuing to lead Grab and create value for Grab and its ecosystem partners. The Grab Board has reviewed and approved his affiliation with the projects.

Given the parties' mutual interest in developing the AI ecosystem in Malaysia, SoftBank Group has agreed in principle to a five-year lock-up in respect of Grab shares that will be held directly by an entity within SoftBank Group, with the lock-up to take effect in accordance with the agreed terms and subject to customary exceptions.

cross_cutting.description: Japan’s SoftBank Group announced on Monday it has signed a joint development agreement (JDA) with Singapore-based digital powerhouse Grab and Malaysian oil and gas firm Petroleum Sarawak (PETROS) to invest US$1 billion in developing AI data centre infrastructure in Sarawak.
cross_cutting.content:
## Softbank, Grab and PETROS invest US$1b in Sarawak AI infrastructure project

- Details
- John Tanner
- Category: Data Centres & Networks
- 408 views

Japan’s SoftBank Group announced on Monday it has signed a joint development agreement (JDA) with Singapore-based digital powerhouse Grab and Malaysian oil and gas firm Petroleum Sarawak (PETROS) to invest US$1 billion in developing AI data centre infrastructure in Sarawak.

Under the JDA – which follows a framework agreement signed by all three companies last month – the multi-year AI infrastructure project has set a long-term target of building 5GW of AI compute capacity.

The project will be led and majority-owned by SoftBank, which will invest US$800 million. Grab and PETROS will serve as strategic partners, with each investing US$100 million. Grab will contribute its digital and AI expertise to the project, while PETROS will leverage its local energy and infrastructure development experience.

The agreement also calls for Softbank, Grab and PETROS to explore opportunities across the wider AI value chain, including AI compute and services, advanced technologies, robotics, local workforce and community development in Sarawak.

Softbank said the proposed US$1 billion investment will be deployed in stages, which will be subject to projects achieving key development and customer contract milestones, as well as the necessary closing conditions.

All three partners will also seek additional investors and hyperscaler customers to support the project's development and long-term expansion.

SoftBank Group chairman and CEO Masayoshi Son said the investment will support Malaysia's ambition to become a regional AI hub, while creating opportunities for Sarawak to diversify its economy and move towards higher-value industries.

“Together with Grab and Petros, we aim to create lasting opportunities in Sarawak and support the development of technology-driven economic activity across Malaysia and the wider region,” Son said in a statement.

Anthony Tan, co-founder, chairman and CEO of Grab, added that Sarawak’s abundant energy resources, established power generation capacity and growing digital economy ambitions provide a strong foundation for the development of large-scale AI infrastructure.

“Sarawak's focus on sustainable energy use and long-term vision make it a natural home for AI infrastructure that can serve all of Southeast Asia,” Tan said.

PETROS group CEO Janin Girie said the project will prepare Sarawak for its next phase of economic transformation beyond oil and gas.

“We want to build a high-income economy where technology and innovation create new industries, opportunities and high-value jobs for Sarawakians,” he said. “By bringing advanced AI and computing capabilities closer to our local businesses, industries and talents, we can strengthen their capabilities, improve competitiveness and enable greater participation in the digital economy.”

# Interactive hosts Dicker Data Cisco AI kit in Sydney
Wed, 11th Nov 2026 (Today) 
MARA SUGUE News Editor

Interactive will host Dicker Data's Cisco AI Rally Kit in its Sydney data centre, giving Dicker Data's partner network access to dedicated AI infrastructure in Australia.

The setup is designed to let eligible partners test and validate AI use cases before committing to production environments of their own. Dicker Data's AI Accelerate programme will use the kit, which combines Cisco infrastructure with NVIDIA GPUs and 120TB of storage from Everpure.

The system will be housed in Interactive's sovereign Sydney facility, providing a local environment for partners to trial workloads involving data privacy, latency and sovereignty considerations. It is aimed at organisations exploring private AI, as well as those undertaking proof-of-concept work.

Partners will be able to test AI ideas and assess the infrastructure needed to support them in practice. Industry-specific use cases will also be available as a starting point for organisations still deciding where AI may fit into their operations.

The arrangement reflects growing interest among Australian businesses in testing AI projects on dedicated local infrastructure rather than moving straight to production. It also points to demand for environments where companies can assess operational and compliance issues alongside technical performance.

David Leen, Head of Product - Cloud at Interactive, said the main challenge for many organisations is not interest in AI but identifying practical uses. "There is no shortage of interest in AI. The harder question for many organisations is understanding where AI can genuinely create value and what it will take to make a use case work in their environment. It means organisations can learn more about what their use case demands before making bigger decisions about the infrastructure required to support it in production," he said.

Testing Demand

For technology partners, access to shared infrastructure can reduce the cost and complexity of early-stage trials. Rather than building their own environment from the outset, partners can use the hosted system to run tests, develop proofs of concept and assess whether a use case is viable.

Interactive's role in the project places its data centre business at the centre of a broader market shift towards sovereign AI services. In Australia, the term is increasingly used to describe AI deployments in which data, infrastructure and operations remain under local control.

Lizzy Jones, Head of Data & AI at Interactive, said infrastructure access is only one part of moving from experimentation to broader adoption. "Successful AI adoption starts with understanding the problem you are trying to solve and the outcome you want to achieve. The ability to then test that thinking against real infrastructure helps organisations understand what works, where the gaps are and what they need to address before moving further," she said.

Jones added that private AI projects require companies to weigh broader design choices before launch. "For private AI in particular, decisions about infrastructure can't be separated from questions around data, security, latency, privacy and sovereignty. Testing a real use case gives organisations a much clearer picture of those requirements before they commit to a production approach," she said.

Sovereign Focus

Dicker Data said the hosted model is intended to help partners explore customer applications across different sectors without additional investment. That may appeal to resellers and integrators looking to shape AI offerings for industries with tighter regulatory requirements or stricter data handling rules.

The project also underlines the role distributors are taking in helping channel partners navigate AI adoption. By combining vendor infrastructure with hosted access and pre-built use cases, they can offer a lower-risk path for partners that want to develop AI services without making large capital commitments upfront.

Vickie Madeleine, General Manager, Cisco at Dicker Data, framed the initiative around security, compliance and operational risk. "Sovereign AI continues to gain momentum with the need to manage data security, compliance, and operational risk more critical than ever. Dicker Data is proud to partner with Interactive, leveraging its sovereign Sydney data centre to deliver secure, scalable, and high-performance infrastructure for AI innovation. We believe this practical and accessible way of experiencing Cisco and Everpure infrastructure and AI-specific use cases will help partners unlock AI opportunities, accelerate their learning journey, and build confidence in deploying AI solutions for their customers," she said.

Interactive, an Australian-owned technology services company, supports more than 2,000 customers across 46,000 locations in Australia and New Zealand. Its business spans cloud, cyber security, data and AI, network services, data centres and hardware maintenance.

Stavian and Midas Capital team up on digital infrastructure

Stavian Group and Midas Capital have agreed to cooperate on submarine cable and digital infrastructure, including infrastructure for AI, in a deal highlighting international efforts to advance Vietnam's high-tech development.

Photo: Stavian Group

The two companies signed an MoU on strategic cooperation in investment and development of submarine cable and digital infrastructure on November 9, with Party General Secretary and State President To Lam witnessing the ceremony. The agreement covers AI infrastructure and aims to strengthen international connectivity and mobilise resources for Vietnam's digital transformation.

The MoU sets out a long-term strategic cooperation framework with an expected total investment of $1 billion across four key areas: developing new submarine cable systems linking Vietnam with international markets, including Japan; building digital and AI infrastructure such as data centres, digital parks, and AI computing facilities; connecting financial resources and international partners; and promoting technology transfer, international operating standards, and high-quality workforce development.

Under the deal, Stavian Group will lead project development and investment procedures in Vietnam, while Midas Capital will help mobilise financial resources, technology partners, and relevant institutions in Japan and internationally. The parties aim to advance specific ventures through further assessment, due diligence, and subsequent implementation agreements.

One of the key digital infrastructure projects is MViSTA, an open submarine cable system designed to connect Vietnam with Malaysia, Singapore, and Thailand. It aims to strengthen international transmission capacity, provide more diverse international data routes, and support the development of data centre, cloud computing, and AI ecosystems in the region.

MViSTA is designed to span approximately 2,500 kilometres, with a capacity of 400 Tbps across 16 fibre pairs. The project involves strategic investors from four countries: Stavian Group (Vietnam), Midas Capital (Japan), OMS Group (Malaysia), and LitUp (Singapore).

Through the subsidiary Stavian Hightech Infrastructure JSC, Stavian Group is also advancing plans for Stavian Digital Park (Stavian DP) in Ho Chi Minh City. Planned across approximately 300 hectares, Stavian DP is planned as a dedicated digital technology zone serving hyperscale cloud service providers, data centres, enterprises, and other organisations requiring digital infrastructure. The project’s feasibility study is funded by the US Trade and Development Agency and led by Cushman & Wakefield, with APTelecom participating as a specialist telecommunications subcontractor.

MViSTA and Stavian DP are envisioned as complementary parts of an integrated digital infrastructure ecosystem, linking international data transmission with data centre facilities and AI computing capabilities. Through these projects, Stavian Group aims to build an integrated digital infrastructure ecosystem that can scale in line with international standards, strengthen connectivity, and support the advancement of high technology in Vietnam.

The MoU between Stavian Group and Midas Capital also reflects the parties' shared commitment to implementing Resolutions No.57-NQ/TW and No.68-NQ/TW, while advancing the Vietnam–Japan Comprehensive Strategic Partnership through infrastructure development, resource mobilisation, and technology transfer.

Speaking at the event, Dinh Duc Thang, chairman of Stavian Group, said digital infrastructure is a fundamental foundation for the development of AI, the digital economy, and national competitiveness.

"Through our cooperation with Midas Capital and international partners, Stavian Group aims to develop submarine cable, data centre, and AI infrastructure projects with connectivity and scalability aligned with international standards," he said. "We expect this cooperation to help connect investment resources, technology, and international expertise, supporting Vietnam's digital infrastructure development and digital transformation while expanding technology cooperation with Japan and other partners across the region."

Cooperation with Midas Capital and the development of MViSTA and Stavian DP see Stavian Group continue to expand its activities in technology and infrastructure, in line with its four core business pillars: Industry, Technology, Energy, and Trade. These initiatives reflect the group's commitment to contributing to Vietnam's digital transformation and the development of its high-tech ecosystem.

cross_cutting.content:
IT Brief UK - Technology news for CIOs & IT decision-makers

# Netcompany backs Danish AI supercomputer with DKK 325m
Tue, 10th Nov 2026 (Today) 
SOFIAH NICHOLE SALIVIO News Editor

Netcompany is investing DKK 325 million in the Danish Centre for AI Innovation, the operator of Denmark's Gefion AI supercomputer. The investment is part of a wider DKK 500 million funding round alongside EIFO and the Novo Nordisk Foundation.

The deal will make Netcompany a new co-owner of DCAI, which runs Gefion, a national AI computing system used by organisations across defence, research, academia, healthcare and industry. EIFO is contributing DKK 150 million in the latest round, while the Novo Nordisk Foundation will remain the majority owner.

After completion, DCAI will be owned 52.6% by the Novo Nordisk Foundation, with EIFO and Netcompany each holding 23.7%. Netcompany Chief Executive Officer André Rogaczewski will also join the company's board of directors.

The fresh capital will be used to expand AI computing infrastructure and related technology, while also building out the organisation behind the platform. The aim is to widen access to what the investors describe as sovereign AI for companies, public bodies and researchers in Denmark.

The investment comes as European governments and companies examine their reliance on foreign-owned technology infrastructure for advanced computing and artificial intelligence. In Denmark, Gefion's backers are positioning the system as domestic infrastructure for sectors where data is sensitive or subject to regulation.

Netcompany says it will bring experience from running critical public sector IT systems, including round-the-clock operations and security work. It will also contribute its Feniks Governance product, which it describes as an orchestration layer that makes raw GPU capacity available as a service.

National focus

Gefion was inaugurated in 2024 and initially focused on training large AI models. Demand has since shifted as organisations look to embed AI into products, services and internal processes, while newer forms of AI software take on more complex tasks.

DCAI describes the facility as Denmark's first AI supercomputer. It operates on an NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD system with 1,528 NVIDIA H100 GPUs.

The latest investment is also tied to Denmark's broader policy goal of becoming a leading country in the development and responsible use of AI. Backers argue that domestic control over computing resources will become more important as AI adoption spreads through regulated industries and public services.

Rogaczewski framed the transaction as part of a wider European effort to retain greater control over strategic technology infrastructure.

"The real value of Gefion will not be measured in computing power alone. It will be measured by what Denmark and Europe are able to build with it. Together with the Novo Nordisk Foundation and EIFO, we want to transform this technological foundation into a national AI capability that enables businesses, researchers and public institutions to develop and deploy AI securely, responsibly and at scale. This is about strengthening Denmark's and Europe's competitiveness, resilience and digital sovereignty, and ensuring that we do not simply participate in the AI revolution, but that we are shaping it," said André Rogaczewski, Chief Executive Officer, Netcompany.

For DCAI, the new funding is intended to support a shift from providing raw computing capacity to offering a system that public and private users can adopt more easily in operational settings.

"When Gefion was inaugurated in 2024, the main task was to train large AI models. Today, companies and public organisations are building AI into their products and workflows, and a new generation of AI agents is taking on more complex tasks. DCAI will now be able to build modern AI capacity that public institutions and businesses can trust and adopt, not least where data is sensitive or regulated," said Martin Svensson, Chief Executive Officer, DCAI.

The government has also linked the project to wider economic and strategic concerns around access to computing power, data and AI systems in Europe.

"With Gefion, we are investing in Europe's digital sovereignty and its ability to compete in a world where access to computing power, data and artificial intelligence is crucial... At the same time, it will strengthen our competitiveness and help ensure that ownership of tomorrow's technology is not left to others," said Martin Lidegaard, Minister for Business and Competitiveness.
